extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency standards executives, agency policy staff, NIST staff, and OMB/reporting officials responsible for implementing OMB Circular A-119 and P.L. 104-113
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reporting requirements for Federal agencies to implement OMB Circular A-119 and the National Technology Transfer and Advancement Act (P.L. 104-113), including use of voluntary consensus standards, participation in standards bodies, conformity assessment coordination, and required agency reporting to NIST/OMB. Targets agency procedures, designated officials, interagency coordination, and metrics for FY reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use voluntary consensus standards except where impractical or inconsistent with law
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with Section 12(d) of the NTTAA, the Circular directs agencies to use voluntary consensus standards in lieu of government-unique standards except where inconsistent with law or otherwise impractical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies are intended to minimize reliance on government-unique standards; agencies should adopt VCS whenever practicable. The Circular's policy does not create discrimination among private-sector standards developers whether or not they are VCS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify use of government-unique standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must justify use of government-unique standards when they are used in lieu of voluntary consensus standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most agencies must make a 'serious attempt' to justify government-unique standards; failure to use an existing standard should be rare (report cited only one failure). Where no applicable VCS exists, agencies should document that fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect and report specified implementation data to NIST/OMB
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must collect specific information regarding the status of implementation: agency use of government-unique standards, data on the use of voluntary consensus standards, the number of voluntary standards substituted for government-unique standards, and the number of individual agency participants in voluntary standards bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information is reported in agency submissions (e.g., Table 1). Agencies should follow the Circular's reporting procedures and provide these metrics for annual NIST reporting to OMB/Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designate an Agency Standards Executive with defined responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Standards Executive must have responsibility for coordinating agency-wide standards-related activities, coordinating implementation of the Circular, and serving on the ICSP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The revised Circular clarifies the role; in 1998 each cabinet department and independent agency designated an Agency Standards Executive. This role includes ensuring agency-wide compliance with legal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of Commerce / NIST coordination responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The NTTAA and the Circular assign policy coordination and implementation tasks to the Secretary of Commerce and specifically to NIST, including issuing guidance on conformity assessment and preparing the annual report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIST provides the Chair and Secretariat for the Interagency Committee on Standards Policy (ICSP) and must submit the annual report to OMB, requiring cooperation from all departments and agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICSP as primary interagency coordination vehicle
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Interagency Committee on Standards Policy (ICSP) to coordinate Federal standards-related activities and implement the NTTAA and OMB Circular A-119.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICSP meetings, working groups, and membership (cabinet departments, independent agencies, Executive Office offices) are used to share issues, draft guidance, and implement policy. NIST chairs the ICSP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage and track agency participation in voluntary standards bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should participate in voluntary consensus standards bodies and track staff participation (number of agency employees participating and number of standards bodies engaged).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies reported metrics (e.g., number of VCS bodies with participation and number of employees) and the ICSP working group examined 'actual' vs 'perceived' declines in participation and distributes surveys to monitor trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for identifying existing standards when proposing regulations/procurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should put procedures into place for identifying existing voluntary consensus standards when proposing new regulations or procurement activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: EPA developed wording for notices of proposed rulemaking to highlight opportunities for using VCS and to invite standards-developing organizations to engage. Agencies should include steps to identify applicable standards during rule/procurement development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alert public and SDOs about opportunities to use/develop standards in rulemaking/procurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should alert the public about proposed regulations and procurement actions that involve voluntary consensus standards, allowing SDOs to bring possible standards activities to the agency's attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's example: develop specific notice wording for proposed rulemakings to draw attention to opportunities for using VCS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate conformity assessment activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretary of Commerce (through NIST) should issue guidance to coordinate Federal conformity assessment activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goals include reducing government cost of developing standards, lowering procurement costs and compliance burden, promoting harmonization, supporting U.S. enterprise growth, and relying on the private sector to supply government needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedite revision and avoid out-of-date references in regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies and SDOs should coordinate to address references to out-of-date standards in regulation and expedite revisions so regulations reference current versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private-sector SDOs instituted briefings with Federal agencies to address out-of-date references; agencies/ICSP working groups should pursue ways to keep regulatory references current.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop agency procedures, templates, and tools for standards management
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies (and NIST) should develop policies, templates, electronic registration forms, and other management tools (e.g., template for strategic standards management, online registration of staff participation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIST promulgated a policy on VCS and a strategic standards management template; developed an electronic form for registering NIST/DOC standards participants online; agencies should adopt similar tools for consistent implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ICSP working groups to address topical standards issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish and use ICSP working groups (e.g., federal procurement, agency participation, regulatory agencies working group (ICSP-RAWG), ISO 9000, ISO 14000, laboratory accreditation, directory/database, standards management) to coordinate action, share lessons learned, and produce guidance or papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working groups should investigate issues (e.g., decline in participation), produce white papers (e.g., EMS white paper), host workshops, and coordinate interagency positions (e.g., lab accreditation recognition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote replacement of government/military specifications with VCS where dual-use exists
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies (e.g., DOD) should review government-unique or military specifications and replace them with voluntary consensus standards where there is a dual-use commercial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOD reviewed 30,000+ military specifications, identified candidates for replacement, adopted thousands of VCS, and installed procedures to prevent future proliferation of military documents. Agencies should work with SDOs to create suitable replacements when overlap exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and maintain technical standards program infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies (e.g., DOE via Order 1300.2A) should establish integrated technical standards programs and supporting infrastructure to manage standards activities and require use of international and national VCS in preference to agency/federal standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic orders should encourage staff participation in VCS committees and incorporate NTTAA/OMB Circular references; DOE updated orders and used workshops to share standards management experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency ethics and participation rules for staff involvement in standards bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must have policies/regulations governing employee participation in external standards-developing activities (e.g., FDA's 21 CFR 10.95).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies should encourage participation that is in the public interest and specify circumstances and limits under which employees can participate, including guidance on ethics and board service waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track specific FY reporting statistics on standards activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Report annual statistics such as: number of voluntary consensus standards bodies with agency participation; number of agency employees participating in VCS bodies; number of additional VCS used in the fiscal year; number of VCS substituted for government-unique standards in the fiscal year; number of government-unique standards used in lieu of VCS in the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY98 example numbers are provided in the report; agencies should supply comparable data for annual reporting cycles to allow monitoring of trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host/participate in public workshops, summits and information exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies and NIST should host and participate in seminars, summits, workshops, and open fora to inform stakeholders about revisions to the Circular, encourage coordination, and share 'lessons learned.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: NIST/OMB seminar on the revised Circular, NIST/ANSI Summit, Federal Technical Standards Workshop; use these fora to reach both agency and private-sector audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate government position on recognition of accreditation bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop consensus on government positions regarding recognition of public- and private-sector laboratory accrediting bodies and recognition/acceptance of accreditation to meet regulatory and procurement needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WGLA and related liaison groups engage with private sector (e.g., NACLA, ILAC) to develop positions and facilitate acceptance and international recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standardized mechanisms to collect/maintain directories of staff participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and follow government-wide guidelines and on-line mechanisms for identifying, collecting and maintaining directories of Federal staff who participate on standards-developing committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICSP working group on directory/database and NIST-developed online registration are vehicles; reconvene working groups to review and revise guidelines.
